End-to-end day-off request flow: resident submission through chief approval into the schedule
Feedback capture-to-triage pipeline: widget/crash capture write, admin function/tab read

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (Cline rule)
nodes.rationale: Forces terse, fragment-style responses to cut filler/fluff and save tokens while keeping technical substance and code exact; auto-suspends for security warnings, irreversible actions, or user confusion, and never applies to code/commits/PRs.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (Copilot rule)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract as the Cline/Windsurf/OpenCode/AGENTS variants, ported to GitHub Copilot's own instructions file so the behavior is consistent across every AI tool configured for this repo.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (OpenCode rule)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract ported to OpenCode's AGENTS.md convention.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (Windsurf rule)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract for Windsurf, marked with 'trigger: always_on' frontmatter so it applies to every session without manual activation.

nodes.label: Caveman Terse-Response Mode (top-level AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: Same terse-response contract as the tool-specific variants, placed at repo root as the generic AGENTS.md convention.

nodes.label: Field-Ready Design System
nodes.rationale: Synced (not authored) from the sibling ems-inventory project so this app visually reads as one family with OMD Response and other UTHealth EM tools; must read instantly in sunlight or a dark cab, so the rule is 'quiet, chunky, high-contrast, utilitarian' with one bold element per screen.

nodes.label: Semantic Palette Tokens & Dark-Mode Constraint
nodes.rationale: Dark mode works by remapping a hard-coded list of literal Tailwind utilities in src/index.css; introducing a new literal palette family (zinc/slate/stone/etc.) would silently render light-mode colors in dark mode, so only 8 allowed families plus semantic tokens may be used.

nodes.label: Typography System (Barlow / Barlow Condensed / JetBrains Mono)
nodes.rationale: font-mono reserved for all data readouts (counts, coverage, dates, shift times) so numeric fields read unambiguously at a glance; font-display reserved for titles/stats to keep hierarchy legible under field conditions.
nodes.norm_label: typography system (barlow / barlow condensed / jetbrains mono)

nodes.label: Accessibility Floor
nodes.rationale: Visible keyboard focus, WCAG-AA contrast on tinted status blocks, labeled form fields, aria-labels on icon-only buttons — non-negotiable baseline given the field-use context.

nodes.label: EM Residency Scheduling Engine (ResidentScheduler.jsx)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately almost all scheduling logic lives in one ~7,860-line file with no module boundaries, so edits should grep for '// ─── SECTION ───' markers rather than trust drifting line numbers; auth/day-off-request surfaces are deliberately kept out of it.

nodes.label: Supabase Cloud Sync (res_state, wide-open RLS)
nodes.rationale: Optional cross-device sync via a hand-rolled fetch-based PostgREST client (no @supabase/supabase-js dependency), one fixed jsonb row, last-write-wins with no merge — an accepted tradeoff for a single coordinator used sequentially, not concurrently, same posture as sibling em-scheduler app.

nodes.label: User Feedback Widget & Admin Tab
nodes.rationale: Insert-only anon-key RLS (deliberately not res_state's wide-open posture) because the feedback table is shared with sibling em-scheduler app via an app_name column; reads only via a password-gated Netlify Function using the service-role key.

nodes.label: Auth, Roles & RLS Security Model
nodes.rationale: Three roles (pending/resident/admin) with self-promotion made impossible by construction (profiles_insert_own pins pending, enforce_profile_role_change_rules blocks self-role-change); RLS is the real security boundary, UI gates are convenience only — a real gap once existed where 'pending' was only checked client-side, enabling impersonation via /requests.

nodes.label: Resident Day-Off Request Feature (residentRequests/ + RequestsTab)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a separate surface from ResidentScheduler.jsx by design — nothing under residentRequests/ imports from it, fetching its own data from the shared res_state row instead, so the ~37-hook scheduling file stays untouched by auth state.

nodes.label: Circadian Scheduling Rules (NIGHT_RULES)
nodes.rationale: Night runs must cluster 4-6 (hard cap 6); eve/day adjacency hard-blocked; ≥24h post-night rest (incl. before Grand Rounds) is deliberately a soft rule, checked in both directions because the generator's optional fill pass can place a night shift after a day shift already scheduled 1-2 days later.

nodes.label: Journal Club Rules (JC_MAX_PER_AY)
nodes.rationale: 'Worked' JC shifts derived from SHIFT_TIMING overlap rather than a hand-maintained shift-id list so PED-S/Trauma Night are automatically covered; cap counted only across Published blocks plus the live block.

nodes.label: Schedule Generator (generateSchedule / fillDayPass)
nodes.rationale: Three-pass fill (min, TRAUMA-D, optional-max) with a candidate pool recomputed fresh per slot — caching once went stale mid-day and caused double-booking, so recomputation is deliberate, not an optimization opportunity.

nodes.label: jspdf-autotable Import Interop Bug
nodes.rationale: jspdf-autotable@3.8.4's default export resolves to a CJS namespace object under esbuild/Rollup bundling, not a callable function; npm run build succeeding does NOT catch this since bundling resolves imports without executing them. Fixed via side-effect import (patches doc.autoTable on) rather than the bare function-call form.

nodes.label: Soft Rule Priority System (appSettings.rulePriority)
nodes.rationale: Chief-orderable ranking of coverageMin/seniorComposition/postNightRest decides whether the generator reaches for a rest-violating or junior candidate versus leaving a slot unfilled — default order favors filling coverage over protecting the other two rules.

nodes.label: Rule-Default Migration (LEGACY_*_DEFAULTS)
nodes.rationale: Chief-saved overrides replace defaults wholesale, so correcting a default entry can be silently masked forever by an old override equal to the previous (wrong) default; LEGACY_*_DEFAULTS snapshots pre-correction shapes so they can be auto-pruned on mount.

nodes.label: RLS Policy Design (resident vs chief scoping)
nodes.rationale: Residents may only INSERT/SELECT their own resident_id rows and UPDATE status pending->cancelled; only a chief profile may SELECT all / decide any row — this is the app's first real per-user RLS, distinct from res_state's wide-open posture.
nodes.norm_label: rls policy design (resident vs chief scoping)

nodes.label: Known Limitation: 'Residents Never See Schedule' is UI-only
nodes.rationale: Consciously accepted, not a bug: /requests reads the same wide-open-RLS res_state row as the chief's cloud sync, so the entire schedule crosses the wire before the UI narrows it; the unauthenticated '/' route can also be visited directly. Closing this for real would need a narrow RLS-scoped view/Edge Function plus real auth on '/' — out of scope for this feature.
nodes.norm_label: known limitation: 'residents never see schedule' is ui-only

nodes.label: feedback Table Schema
nodes.rationale: A brand-new table structurally unrelated to res_state's single-row document (needs many independent rows), so it deliberately does not reuse res_state's sync machinery; carries app_name so a future em-scheduler feedback feature on the same shared project can't collide.

nodes.label: Crash Auto-Capture (window.onerror/unhandledrejection)
nodes.rationale: Deduped per session via sessionStorage (message + first stack line) and capped at 5 auto-reports per session so a tight error loop can't flood the feedback table.

nodes.label: Track A: Shared-Password Admin Gating
nodes.rationale: This app has no auth system of its own (whoever has the URL/env vars has full read-write to res_state), so a shared server-checked password is the only viable admin gate — matches the same pattern used by sibling Kitchen Inventory and ecowater-pricing-app.

nodes.label: Task 2: profiles + day_off_requests Schema & RLS
nodes.rationale: BEFORE UPDATE triggers (enforce_resident_id_immutable, enforce_cancel_only_status) close gaps plain RLS WITH CHECK can't express, e.g. WITH CHECK alone can't guarantee 'no other column changed' during a cancel, and IS DISTINCT FROM (not =/!=) is required so NULL columns don't defeat the guard.

nodes.label: Task 3: Server-Side Email-Domain Signup Restriction
nodes.rationale: A client-side-only domain check is trivially bypassed by calling Supabase's auth REST API directly with the public anon key (visible in this public repo's deployed bundle regardless), so enforcement must live in a Postgres 'Before User Created' Auth Hook.

nodes.label: Task 9: Chief-Side Requests Tab (Login/Role Gate)
nodes.rationale: ApprovalQueue is deliberately a separate component, not inlined into RequestsTab's conditional-return body, because placing its hooks after early returns that fire conditionally across renders would violate the Rules of Hooks.

nodes.label: Task 10: Chief Approve/Deny Actions (ApprovalQueue)
nodes.rationale: Approval writes straight into the resident's existing approvedDatesOff array, the exact field getEligibleShifts/the generator/the grid already treat as a hard block — so no changes to the eligibility/generator engine are needed.

nodes.label: Task 12: Email Notifications (Resend Edge Function)
nodes.rationale: Fails soft — a Resend error is logged, not thrown, so a flaky email provider never blocks the underlying database write that triggered the webhook (fired after the write already committed).

nodes.label: Task 1: feedback Schema, submitFeedback, app_version
nodes.rationale: prefer: 'return=minimal' is required on insert because Postgres RLS only returns an INSERT...RETURNING row if a SELECT policy also grants read access, and anon deliberately has none on this table.

nodes.label: Task 4: feedback-admin Netlify Function + netlify.toml
nodes.rationale: The /api/feedback-admin/* redirect must be placed before the SPA catch-all /* redirect in netlify.toml, since Netlify redirects are matched top-to-bottom; reversed order would serve index.html for every function call.

nodes.label: Task 5: Feedback Admin Tab (Password-Gated Triage UI)
nodes.rationale: The 'feedback' entry stays a fixed member of the static TABS array (so reconcileTabOrder/backup-restore keep working unchanged) and is instead filtered out of SidebarNav's rendering when cloud sync is off, rather than being conditionally omitted from TABS itself.

nodes.label: Vite %VITE_*% HTML Token Injection into window globals
nodes.rationale: Env vars are injected via Vite's %VITE_*% HTML token substitution into window.__SUPABASE_URL__/__SUPABASE_ANON__/__ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAIN__ rather than import.meta.env directly, so client code must treat the literal unresolved '%VITE_...%' string (not empty string) as 'not configured'.
